finding.blocking_rationale: This is a critical data loss defect that violates a mandatory requirement (REQ-2) and realizes an unacceptable risk (RISK-1: stored listings or their price history are lost or silently altered during normal operation). The defect occurs during normal operation (rescraping) and causes irreversible data loss. It must be resolved before the controlled-validation stage because the validation will collect price history data that will be lost, making the validation results unreliable.
finding.description: upsert_listing uses INSERT OR REPLACE to store a listing. When a listing with the same (backend, external_id) already exists, INSERT OR REPLACE deletes the old row and inserts a new one. The price_history table has a foreign key on listing_id with ON DELETE CASCADE (schema.py:41). When the old listing row is deleted, all its price_history rows are cascade-deleted. This means every time a scraper rescrapes a listing with a different price, the previous price observations are lost. The new price is appended to price_history, but the history now contains only the new price, not the full history of price changes.
finding.evidence: Reproduction: Open a store, upsert_listing a listing at price 649€ at time T0. Upsert the same listing at price 599€ at time T1. Call price_history('kleinanzeigen', '1'). Result: only one entry with price_minor=59900 at T1. The entry for 64900 at T0 was deleted. Direct inspection of the price_history table shows only one row with listing_id=1 after the rescrape, confirming the old rows were cascade-deleted when INSERT OR REPLACE deleted the old listing row. The listing_id is reused (autoincrement), but the old price_history rows pointing to it are gone.
finding.impact: Inside the operating envelope, scrapers rescrape listings regularly. Every rescrape with a price change loses the previous price history. This violates the requirement that price_history returns the first price followed by every later change. Buyers relying on price history to track price drops will see incomplete history. The defect affects all listings ingested via upsert_listing, which is the primary ingestion path for live scrapes.
finding.title: upsert_listing loses price history on rescrape due to INSERT OR REPLACE with CASCADE DELETE
finding.verification: Fix upsert_listing to use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (backend, external_id) DO UPDATE instead of INSERT OR REPLACE, preserving the existing row's id and avoiding the CASCADE DELETE. Alternatively, disable CASCADE DELETE and handle history cleanup explicitly. Verify by: (1) upsert a listing at price 649€ at T0, (2) upsert the same listing at price 599€ at T1, (3) call price_history and assert it returns two entries: 64900 at T0 and 59900 at T1. Run the existing test suite to ensure no regressions.
